info.title: Wavefunction Local API
info.description: Local desktop coding agent with independent conversations

schema.title: Response List Skills Api Skills Get

post.description:
Write a new skill.

The name is derived from the title unless one is given, because a title is what someone
types and the spec's name rules are not something they should have to know.

put.description: Change a skill. Renaming is refused: tasks capture a skill by its name.

delete.description: Remove a skill from the library.

post.description: `gh auth login` with GitHub's device flow; the card polls for its one-time code.

get.description:
Whether Google's console has just saved a Desktop client file to Downloads.

Its name, never its contents: the form offers it so nobody has to find it in a file chooser.

schema.title: Response Connector Catalog Api Connector Catalog Get
Response Catalog Connection Status Api Connector Catalog Connections Get

get.description:
The MCP servers you have added, and what each is offering.

Connected services supply tools to the next coding task.

schema.title: Response List Connectors Api Connectors Get

post.description: Add a server and ask it what it offers, so a failure is visible now rather than at run.

Ask a URL what it is and what signing in to it takes.

Someone adding a connector knows a URL. Whether it speaks streamable HTTP or SSE, whether the
path is /mcp or /sse, and whether it wants a token or a browser round trip are all things the
server will say if it is asked — so they are asked here rather than put to the user as
settings they would have to look up.

put.description:
Save the value behind a `$NAME` written in a connector's settings.

Kept apart from the settings themselves so the token lives in the credentials file rather
than in the connector list, which is plain JSON in the app's own settings.

Change a server's settings and try it again straight away.

Renaming is refused rather than handled: agents bind a tool by `server__tool`, and a rename
would quietly break every one of them. Remove and re-add is the honest way to do that.

delete.description: Remove a server and its tools.

post.description: Ask a server what it offers now. Its tools change when the server does.

Open a browser and complete this server's OAuth flow.

Blocks while the user is signing in — the round trip ends when they come back, which is the
honest shape for something that waits on a person. Tokens land in the secret store.
Forget this server's tokens. The next sign-in starts the flow again.
The GitHub card finished signing gh in: the task waiting on it carries on.
The folder the user picked on a folder card: where the agent works, or one a task needs.

get.description:
Whether computer use can run: Docker installed, engine running, image built.

`refresh=true` probes Docker; without it the cached status is returned, because the
settings page polls this while a build streams and a probe per poll would be noise.

post.description: Start building the desktop image. Follow progress by polling GET /api/computer.

get.description:
Serve one stored screenshot to the trace view.

The webview's CSP allows only blob and data images, so the frontend fetches this with the
bearer token and displays the blob — the file itself never gets a public URL.

put.description: Require zero data retention from OpenRouter and the Vercel AI Gateway, for chats started after.

get.description:
What the desktop shell shows next. It asks again with the cursor this returned, waiting up to
`wait` seconds for a task to end or pause when there is nothing yet.

post.description: Use the same capability information as model construction, without making a model call.

get.description:
What the Vercel AI Gateway offers.

Listed without a key, unlike OpenRouter's: the catalogue is public, so someone can see that
the model they want is reachable before deciding to connect.
The Claude models the saved Anthropic key can use, with what each request may send.
The Gemini models the saved key can use for chat.

post.description:
Begin a ChatGPT sign-in and return the URL to open.

The listener is up before this answers, so the browser cannot beat it.
Forget the sign-in. Chats on a `codex` model stop running until one is signed in again.

put.description: Set the model new chats start on.

delete.description:
Forget a provider or search key. As with signing out of ChatGPT, its models stay enabled
and run again once a key is back; until then a chat on one says which key to connect.

Connector.title: Connector
Connector.description: A connector in the list, with its saved keys and what it last offered.

Draft.title: Draft
Draft.description: The message a fork or rewind put back in the composer.

GrantCreate.title: GrantCreate
GrantCreate.description:
One outside folder the user makes available to coding tasks.

Grants never come from a spec. A model may say an agent uses a write tool; it may never
decide which paths that reaches.

McpServer.title: McpServer
McpServer.description:
One connected MCP server.

`stdio` runs a command on this machine; `http` talks to a URL. The difference matters beyond
transport: a command can only ever run where this app runs, so an agent using its tools
cannot be deployed anywhere else. `reachable_when_deployed` is what says so.

ModelChoice.title: ModelChoice
ModelChoice.description:
A saved ModelSpec. A chat's model is saved as its settings sent it, so the fields
after `model` can be missing, as `reasoning_effort` is from the built-in default.

reasoning_effort.title: Reasoning Effort
reasoning_effort.description: Provider default when omitted. Use a supported effort level, or enabled/none for a model with a thinking toggle.

Routine.title: Routine
Routine.description: A chat sent `instruction` on a schedule while the app is open.

SavedConnector.title: SavedConnector
SavedConnector.description: A connector just added or changed, and whether it answered.

SetupRow.title: SetupRow
SetupRow.description: A row of a paused task's setup card: a connector, folder, GitHub or computer use.

SidebarThread.title: SidebarThread
SidebarThread.description: A chat as the sidebar lists it: with its routine and the state of its runs.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description: Provider-reported totals. Cache and reasoning counts are subsets, not extra tokens.
